sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Construct described as expressed in HEK293 cells for protein-interaction studies; no dedicated surface-expression or functional assay for the FLAG-tagged construct is reported in the ledger.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the FLAG tag was inserted 'after the signal peptide of LRP10'. The signal peptide spans residues 1–16 (landmark-authoritative), so the junction is after residue 16 (A) and before residue 17 (H), the mature extracellular N-terminus. Python confirmed seq[16]='A' and seq[17]='H'. The site is 424 residues from the TM boundary (441), well within the large extracellular domain, and is the only extracellular terminus of this single-pass type-I receptor. Full-length human LRP10 in pcDNA3.1; PCR-based mutagenesis used to insert a FLAG tag explicitly 'after the signal peptide of LRP10' (signal peptide = residues 1–16, mature N-terminus = residue 17 H). Construct expressed in HEK293 cells.

sources.claim: LRP10 was subcloned in the pcDNA3.1 vector, and PCR - based mutagenesis was used to insert an HA-tag at the C-terminus of LRP10 or a FLAG-tag after the signal peptide of LRP10.
Another V5 tag was introduced into the N-terminal position relative to the LRP10 insert.

literature_notes: Four ledger lines were examined. L1 and L3 both describe N-terminal extracellular tags on full-length human LRP10 and yield two sites at the same junction (after residue 16), grounded in different papers and tag types, so both are reported. L1 also describes a C-terminal HA tag and L2 confirms its use in immunoprecipitation; both are intracellular (residue 713 lies in the cytoplasmic tail, residues 462–713) and are recorded in other_positions. L4 describes a C-terminal HA on full-length mouse Lrp10, also intracellular by the same topology, and is likewise recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for LRP10.

literature_other_positions.note: HA tag inserted at the C-terminus of full-length human LRP10 (residue 713); the C-terminus lies in the intracellular tail (residues 462–713) and is not accessible on the extracellular face.

C-terminal HA tag on full-length mouse Lrp10 expressed in heterologous cells; the C-terminus is intracellular by the conserved single-pass type-I topology, confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation use only.
